question: Why can the last portion of karma not be cut off?
premises: The final ten cannot be cut off.
To restrain them in this very body is impossible.
Whatever else is there, new or ancient, remains in the same body.
inference: The last stretch of begun karma must run its course in this body, whether freshly made or old.
uncertainties: antyadaśa ('the last ten') may be a tenth-part idiom or a literal ten; the basis of the count is not stated here.
plain_english: The last ten cannot be cut off; to restrain them is not possible, in that same body, whatever else there is, today's or ancient.
